gold.description: Invalid Zod schema syntax. Computed property keys like [z.string().toString()] are not valid in Zod object schemas and will cause runtime errors.

candidate.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema`'s computed keys collapse to a single literal key; the expiry claim is never enforced
candidate.description: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both produce `"[object Object]"`, so the schema has only one dynamic key which overwrites expiry, causing tokens to be treated as permanently expired.

gold.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Pers
gold.description: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

candidate.title: Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with the zod result wrapper, not the parsed key
candidate.description: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result wrapper instead of just the parsed object, so prisma writes `{success:true,data:{...}}` into `Credential.key`, causing parsing to fail on next load and breaking Google Calendar permanently.

gold.title: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the
gold.description: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

candidate.title: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` Response in the sharing branch, but four callers expect an SDK/axios shape
candidate.description: Helper returns raw Response when credential sync enabled, but callers expect parsed body properties like `.data`, causing credential sync to fail for googlecalendar, hubspot, zohocrm, zoho-bigin.

missed_correctness_gold.title: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's
missed_correctness_gold.description: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

missed_correctness_gold.title: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.acc
missed_correctness_gold.description: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

promotion_candidates.title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects `userId`
promotion_candidates.description: Passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to sync endpoint, causing it to resolve to wrong user and return another account's access token or none.

promotion_candidates.title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every instantiation, then builds the connection with the stale one
promotion_candidates.description: Token refreshed unconditionally on every construction without expiry check, but connection built with old token values before refresh completes, making refresh ineffective and adding unnecessary network calls.
